identity.title: Nuchal rigidity (neck stiffness on passive flexion)

technique.how: With the patient supine and relaxed, cradle the occiput and passively flex the neck toward the chest. Positive if there is involuntary resistance or pain that limits flexion; check rotation and lateral flexion, which stay relatively free in meningeal irritation but not in cervical spine disease.
technique.prerequisites: Patient relaxed (can be done in obtunded patients); cervical spine cleared if trauma possible.
technique.contraindications: Possible cervical spine injury or atlantoaxial instability.

interpretation.positive_finding: Present in roughly half of adults with CSF pleocytosis (pooled sensitivity 0.46, specificity 0.71, LR+ 1.6); it modestly raises the probability and supports LP.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence gives LR- about 0.76 and does not exclude meningitis (sensitivity 0.13-0.30 in two prospective adult cohorts). Sensitivity approached 1.0 only with severe pleocytosis (>=1000 WBC, n=4).
interpretation.pitfalls: Older patients with cervical spondylosis or parkinsonism have stiff necks without meningitis; drowsy or immunocompromised patients often lack the sign. The RCE's 99-100% figure is for the triad (fever, neck stiffness or altered mental status), not neck stiffness alone.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: lower threshold for LP and empiric antibiotics; negative: still LP if fever with headache or altered mental status.

estimates.target_condition: Nuchal rigidity for CSF pleocytosis (meningitis) in suspected meningitis
estimates.population: Adults with suspected meningitis undergoing LP; 9 case-control datasets (599 with pleocytosis, 1216 without), mostly Japan/Iran

estimates.target_condition: Nuchal rigidity for meningitis (>=6 WBC/mL CSF)
estimates.population: 297 adults with suspected meningitis evaluated before LP, single US center
estimates.quote: nuchal rigidity (sensitivity, 30%; LR(+), 0.94) did not accurately discriminate between patients with meningitis (>/=6 white blood cells [WBCs]/mL

estimates.target_condition: Nuchal rigidity for severe meningeal inflammation (>=1000 WBC/mL CSF)
estimates.population: Subset of 4 patients with severe pleocytosis among 297 adults with suspected meningitis
estimates.quote: Only for 4 patients with severe meningeal inflammation (>/=1000 WBCs/mL of CSF) did nuchal rigidity show diagnostic value (sensitivity, 100%; negative predictive value, 100%)

estimates.target_condition: Nuchal rigidity for CSF pleocytosis (>=5 cells/hpf)
estimates.population: 230 neurologically intact ED adults undergoing LP, altered mental status excluded; 2 inner-city academic EDs
estimates.reference_standard: CSF pleocytosis >=5 cells/high-power field in 4th tube
estimates.quote: Brudzinski sign was 2%, and nuchal rigidity was 13% ... Brudzinski sign was 98%, and nuchal rigidity was 80%

estimates.target_condition: Composite: at least one of fever, neck stiffness or altered mental status, for acute meningitis
estimates.population: Adults with objectively confirmed bacterial or viral meningitis across included studies (children and immunocompromised excluded)
estimates.quote: the absence of fever, neck stiffness, and altered mental status effectively eliminates meningitis (sensitivity, 99%-100% for the presence of 1 of these findings)

sources.citation: Akaishi T, Kobayashi J, Abe M, et al. Sensitivity and specificity of meningeal signs in patients with meningitis. J Gen Fam Med 2019;20:193-198.
Thomas KE, Hasbun R, Jekel J, Quagliarello VJ. The diagnostic accuracy of Kernig's sign, Brudzinski's sign, and nuchal rigidity in adults with suspected meningitis. Clin Infect Dis 2002;35:46-52.
Nakao JH, Jafri FN, Shah K, Newman DH. Jolt accentuation of headache and other clinical signs: poor predictors of meningitis in adults. Am J Emerg Med 2014;32:24-28.
Attia J, Hatala R, Cook DJ, Wong JG. The rational clinical examination. Does this adult patient have acute meningitis? JAMA 1999;282:175-181.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use an absent sign to withhold LP or antibiotics in suspected meningitis; avoid forced flexion in possible cervical injury.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Fever with altered mental status or petechial rash needs immediate cultures and empiric antibiotics irrespective of neck findings.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Akaishi 2019 notes that grading mild stiffness is difficult even for trained clinicians and heterogeneity across studies likely reflects differing thresholds.

extraction_notes: Akaishi 2019 Table 2 from PMC full text (99% CIs, simple pooling of case-control datasets). Thomas 2002 abstract gives sensitivity and LR+ but not specificity (left null). Attia 1999 sensitivity 0.99 is a composite of three findings and was entered separately with the composite named as target; the RCE did not pool nuchal rigidity alone. Nakao 2014 quote joins two abstract fragments with an ellipsis; prevalence 0.20 = 47/230.
